"""A partial lexical-completion model of this component.

Predict fixed pulses when split G-prefixed technical abbreviations finish,
with a negative pulse for GSSG. Also recognize selected split earth/place
terms, Japanese air-temperature vocabulary, and document-formatting cues.
Use a small negative baseline at document starts, zero elsewhere. The
coefficients are empirical pulse heights; other multilingual responses
are not modeled. No earlier document's context is retained.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# The key is the continuation after a G/g prefix (case insensitive).
G_CONTINUATIONS = {
    'cd': 3.4,      # greatest common divisor
    'cf': 2.7,      # greatest common factor
    'dp': 4.0,      # gross domestic product
    'tp': 4.4,      # guanosine triphosphate
    'mp': 5.5,      # guanosine monophosphate / multiple precision
    'fp': 2.2,      # green fluorescent protein
    'sh': 1.8,      # reduced glutathione
    'ss': -2.9,     # oxidized glutathione, GSSG
    'str': 2.6,     # goods and services tax return
    'son': 4.4,     # Gson JSON software
    'df': 1.1,      # GDF file format
    'ce': 2.6,      # general certificate of education
    'te': 2.1,      # greater-than-or-equal comparison
    'sm': 1.1,      # global system for mobile communications
    'to': 0.6,      # Gaussian-type orbital
    'ps': 1.2,      # global positioning system
}


# Completion of split earth/place vocabulary; coefficients differ by word.
PLACE_COMPLETIONS = {
    '圖': 3.2,    # 地圖: map
    '鐵': 4.0,    # 地鐵: underground railway
    '熱': 3.3,    # 地熱: geothermal heat
    '點': 2.3,    # 地點: place
    '名': 1.3,    # 地名: place name
    '主': 2.2,    # 地主: landowner
    '上的': 3.2,  # 地上的: on the ground
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    new = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if new else carry[1]
    previous_was_first = False if new else carry[2]
    value = -0.21 if new else 0.0

    if re.search(r'(?:^|[^A-Za-z])[Gg]$', previous):
        value = G_CONTINUATIONS.get(text.lower(), 0.0)
    elif re.search(r'(?:^|[^A-Za-z])Q$', previous) and text == 'CD':
        value = 3.8  # quantum chromodynamics
    if previous == '地':
        value = PLACE_COMPLETIONS.get(text, 0.0)
    if previous == '気' and text == '温':
        value = 4.0  # 気温: air temperature
    if text.strip() == 'GDP':
        value = 2.2
    if previous == 'Title' and previous_was_first and text == ':':
        value = 9.466
    if new and text == '//\n':
        value = 3.314  # source-file comment header
    if text and set(text) == {'·'} and previous and set(previous) == {'·'}:
        value = 0.55
    if text == '\xa0' and len(previous) >= 3 and set(previous) == {'\xa0'}:
        value = 0.33
    return (doc, text, new), value

"""A coarse lexical response, mostly confined to document openings.

At an opening, estimate activation from whitespace/code shape, English
frequency, case, and function-word class. Keep the estimate for an initial
run of identical tokens. Otherwise predict zero, except at the second digit
of possible 19xx/20xx years. Reset at document boundaries. These broad rules
do not capture every opening word's individual response.
"""
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

# Adjustments for grammatical/code classes: no leading space / leading space.
WORD_CLASSES = (
    ({'the'}, -0.49, 0.19),                         # definite article
    ({'a', 'an'}, -1.57, -2.75),                   # indefinite article
    (set(('i me my mine we us our ours you your yours he him his '
          'she her hers it its they them their theirs').split()), 0.85, 0.49),
    (set(('in on at to of for from with by about into onto over under '
          'after before between among through during without within').split()),
     -0.82, -1.30),                               # prepositions
    (set('and or but because if although while unless until since as than so'.split()),
     -0.11, -0.53),                               # conjunctions
    (set('am is are was were be been being'.split()), 1.27, 2.20),
    (set(('have has had do does did can could will would shall should '
          'may might must').split()), 0.57, 1.28), # auxiliaries
    (set('what who whom whose where when why how which'.split()), -0.80, -0.34),
    (set('package module namespace'.split()), 4.36, 4.38),
    ({'import', 'from'}, 1.99, 1.85),
)


def opening(token):
    s = token.strip()
    spaced = token.startswith(' ')
    linebreak = '\n' in token or '\r' in token
    if not s:
        if linebreak:
            return -0.9 + 0.8 * spaced
        if '\t' in token:
            return 1.8
        return 2.0 + 1.5 * (min(len(token), 3) - 1)
    if token == '<|endoftext|>':
        return -2.1
    if token.startswith(('<|', '<tool_', '</tool_')):
        return 4.9
    if token == '\\':
        return 6.5

    word = s.lower()
    value = 0.18 + 1.45 * spaced + 0.50 * linebreak
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Latin}+', s):
        frequency = max(0, zipf_frequency(word, 'en') - 3)
        value += -0.38 + 0.06 * min(len(s), 12) - 1.07 * spaced
        value -= frequency * (0.39 + 0.22 * (not spaced))
        value -= 0.42 * s[0].isupper() + 1.00 * (len(s) == 1)
        value += 0.46 * (s.isupper() and len(s) > 1)
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Cyrillic}', s):
        value -= 1.15
    if s.isdecimal():
        value -= 3.73
        if len(s) == 1 and s.isascii():
            value += 0.70 * int(s) / 9
    if all(c in '.,;:!?。！？，；：' for c in s):
        value -= 0.61
    if s in {'.', ','}:
        value += -2.21 + 0.80 * ('\n' in token)
    if all(c in '()[]' for c in s):
        value -= 0.37
    value += 2.19 * any(c in token for c in '_=\\{}')
    value += 0.55 * (s.startswith('.') and len(s) > 1 and s[1].isalpha())
    value += 0.66 * ('"' in s or "'" in s)
    value += 0.44 * all(c in '+-*/^&|<>' for c in s)
    if all(c == '#' for c in s):
        value -= 3.41 / len(s)
    value += 1.92 * (s.startswith('//') or s.startswith('/*'))
    for words, plain, with_space in WORD_CLASSES:
        if word in words:
            value += with_space if spaced else plain
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token, doc = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1]
    digit = token.isascii() and token.isdigit()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        value = opening(token)
        return (doc, token, True, value, token if digit else ''), float(value)
    _, first, initial_run, initial_value, number = carry
    initial_run = initial_run and token == first
    number = (number + token)[-5:] if digit else ''
    value = initial_value if initial_run else {'19': 0.50, '20': 0.20}.get(number, 0.0)
    return (doc, first, initial_run, initial_value, number), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, hidden unit 3009: a document-opening detector.

What it does. The unit is nearly silent inside a document and speaks mainly at the first
token of each document, where the model's attention sees only that token. There its
value depends on what kind of token opens the document:

* English prose openers are negative. Articles and prepositions most of all: "a" (-5.5),
  capitalised "A", "In", "For", "On", "The" (-4.5), spaced " in", " for", " and", " of"
  (-3). Wh-words and "Today" are about -5 when capitalised. Other capitalised words are
  about -2.5, digits -3.5, short lowercase fragments -2. Pronouns are mildly negative.
  Sentence punctuation "." "," "#" is -3.
* Copulas and auxiliaries (" is", " was", " be", " will") are slightly positive (+1).
* Code, markup and layout openers are positive: indentation and tab runs (+4), the chat
  tag "<|im_start|>" (+5), backslashes, "$", underscores, "/*" and "//" (+3), spaced
  brackets and quotes such as ' ("' (+1.5), programming words such as "package", "import",
  "function" (+4), and long unspaced lowercase words (+2).

Inside a document it is otherwise near zero, with three small exceptions: the middle-dot
leader "··" is a constant +2, "9" right after "1" ("19xx" years) is +0.4, and "0" right
after "2" is +0.15.

Why. The sign separates prose from code at the start of a document, which is the
component's main job. Measured on 1024 eval rows it explains about 46% of the activation
variance (Pearson r 0.70). Switching it off or replacing it with this program moves the
next-token distribution by similar amounts (kl_fraction 0.87), because most of the
remaining effect sits at mid-document positions that are too noisy to predict by concept.
An exact per-token table for document openers would explain about 79% of the variance in
the training sample; this rule-based version keeps only the coarse categories.
"""

READS = ()

ARTICLE_PREP = set("a an the in on at for of to and or with by from as if".split())
WH_WORDS = set("what how today why when where which who first best".split())
PRONOUN = set("i you he she we they it my your our their this that".split())
COPULA = set("is was be are were will".split())
CODE_WORDS = set(
    "package import function const export return class def use include string data type "
    "module path api url image sqlite".split()
)
CODE_SYMBOLS = set("\\$_{}/*=<>&|^`")
PROSE_PUNCT = set(".,#\"')(:")


def opener_value(s):
    """Activation at a document's first token s (its text, decoded alone)."""
    word = s.strip()
    if word == "":
        if "\n" in s:
            return -1.0
        return 4.0 if (len(s) > 1 or "\t" in s) else 2.0
    if s == "<|im_start|>":
        return 5.0
    if word.isdigit():
        return -3.5
    if word.isascii() and word.isalpha():
        spaced = s.startswith(" ")
        low = word.lower()
        if low in COPULA:
            return 1.0
        if low in ARTICLE_PREP:
            if word == "a" and spaced:
                return -5.5
            if word[0].isupper():
                return -4.5
            if word == "the" and spaced:
                return -1.5
            return -3.0 if spaced else -2.0
        if low in WH_WORDS:
            return -5.0 if word[0].isupper() else -2.0
        if low in PRONOUN:
            return -1.5
        if low in CODE_WORDS:
            return 4.0
        if word[0].isupper():
            return -2.5
        if not spaced and len(word) >= 6:
            return 2.0
        if len(word) <= 2:
            return -2.0
        return 0.0
    if word in PROSE_PUNCT:
        if s.startswith(" "):
            return 1.5
        return -3.0 if word in ".,#" else -1.0
    if any(c in CODE_SYMBOLS for c in word):
        return 3.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: (position within the current document, previous token string)."""
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    n, prev = carry if carry is not None else (0, "")
    if len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        n = 0
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if n == 0:
        value = opener_value(s)
    elif s == "··":
        value = 2.0
    elif s == "9" and prev == "1":
        value = 0.4
    elif s == "0" and prev == "2":
        value = 0.15
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (n + 1, s), value

"""Estimate the negative signal at the end of an aside.

Negative values mark commas closing inserted phrases, prose parentheses,
and paired dashes. The strongest values mark a quotation resuming after
a short speaker attribution. Sentence-initial connectives are not asides.
Ordinary text and code punctuation stay near zero. Only a short, document-
local text buffer is kept; this is a surface approximation, not a parser.
"""
import re

READS = ()
CONNECTIVE = re.compile(
    r'(?:however|therefore|nevertheless|nonetheless|moreover|indeed|though|'
    r'of course|for (?:example|instance)|in (?:fact|particular|short|reality)|'
    r'on the (?:other hand|contrary)|after all|at (?:least|any rate)|'
    r'as (?:a (?:result|consequence)|such|well)|rather|anyway|'
    r'certainly|surely|apparently|perhaps|fortunately|unfortunately|alas|actually|'
    r'(?:strictly|generally) speaking|it seems|in turn|'
    r'again|then|say|first|second|finally|thus|otherwise|instead|'
    r'you (?:know|see)|I (?:think|believe|suppose|mean|guess)|'
    r'that is|so to speak|to be (?:sure|fair|honest)|'
    r'é claro|por (?:exemplo|supuesto)|sin embargo|par exemple|bien sûr)$',
    re.I,
)
REPORT = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:said|says|say|added|adds|replied|continued|noted|wrote|writes|'
    r'explained|stated|asked|answered|remarked|reported|believe|think|'
    r'suppose|argued|suggested|agreed|warned|pointed out|shown|mentioned|'
    r'expected|known|described|indicated|told|tells|thought|thinks|claimed|claims|'
    r'observed|observes|cried|cry|announced|acknowledged|hoped|believed)\b', re.I,
)
QUALIFIER = re.compile(
    r'^(?:who|whom|whose|which|including|especially|particularly|notably|'
    r'namely|mostly|mainly|according to|such as|as|like)\b', re.I,
)
# Symbol-heavy fragments are more likely code or formulae than prose asides.
SYMBOLS = re.compile(r'[{}=;\\\[\]<>_]|[a-z][A-Z]')
CLOSING_QUOTE = re.compile(r'([,!?.])["”’»]')
DASH = re.compile(r'[—–]| --? ')


def predict(text, token):
    s = token.strip()
    if not s or '\n' in token:
        return 0.0
    if not (s in (',', '.', '?', '—', '–', '--', '-', '"', '“', '‘', '«')
            or (s.endswith((')', '）', ']')) and '(' not in s)):
        return 0.0
    sentence = re.split(r'[.!?;\n]', text)[-1]
    segment = sentence.rsplit(',', 1)[-1].strip()
    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', segment)
    inserted = ',' in sentence
    if s == ',':
        if not inserted:
            return 0.05
        if (len(segment) < 15 and REPORT.search(segment)
                and re.match(r'^(?:I|we|he|she|they|it|you|one)\b', segment, re.I)):
            return -6.5
        if CONNECTIVE.fullmatch(segment):
            return -4.75 if len(re.findall(r'\w+', sentence)) < 8 else -3.5
        if QUALIFIER.search(segment):
            return -0.9
        if text and text[-1].isdigit():
            return -0.04
        if len(words) > 7:
            return -0.13
        if REPORT.search(segment):
            return -3.55 if len(segment) < 15 else -1.05
        if SYMBOLS.search(segment):
            return -0.04
        return -0.48 if segment[:1].islower() else -0.21
    if s.endswith((')', '）', ']')):
        closing = s[-1]
        opening = {')': '(', '）': '（', ']': '['}[closing]
        k = text.rfind(opening)
        prose_open = k > 0 and bool(re.search(r'[A-Za-z] $', text[:k]))
        if closing == '）':
            return -0.76 if k >= 0 else -0.07
        if not prose_open:
            return -0.07 if closing == ')' else 0.0
        if closing == ']':
            return -0.33
        inside = text[k+1:]
        long_words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]{4,}', inside)
        code = bool(re.search(r'[{}=;\\]', text[-120:]))
        if len(long_words) >= 2:
            if re.search(r'[=+*/_^{}\\]', inside):
                return -0.2
            return -0.67 if code else -1.4
        return -0.25 if code else -0.67
    if s in ('—', '–', '--', '-'):
        if s == '-' and token != ' -':
            return 0.0
        # A range or minus sign is not a closing parenthetical dash.
        if text.rstrip()[-1:].isdigit():
            return 0.0
        if re.search(r'[{}=;\\]', sentence):
            return 0.0
        marks = list(DASH.finditer(sentence))
        if marks:
            aside = sentence[marks[-1].end():]
            if len(re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]{3,}', aside)) >= 1:
                return -1.0 if s == '-' else -1.6
        return 0.03 if s in ('—', '–') else 0.0
    if s in ('"', '“', '‘', '«') and token.startswith(' '):
        marks = list(CLOSING_QUOTE.finditer(text))
        if marks:
            m = marks[-1]
            tail = text[m.end():]
            core = tail.strip(' .,!?:;\n')
            n = len(re.findall(r'\w+', core))
            immediate = (len(tail) < 100 and 1 <= n <= 12
                         and not re.search(r'["“”.!?;\n]', core))
            if immediate and m.group(1) != '.':
                if text.rstrip().endswith(','):
                    return -7.0
                if text.rstrip().endswith(('.', ';')):
                    return -4.9
            if (len(tail) < 120 and not re.search(r'["“”]', tail)
                    and REPORT.search(tail)):
                return -2.1
        if text.rstrip().endswith('.'):
            return -0.65 if re.search(r'["“”‘’«»]', text[-200:]) else -0.18
    if s in ('.', '?') and inserted:
        if CONNECTIVE.fullmatch(segment):
            return -1.2
        if REPORT.search(segment) and len(segment) < 30:
            return -1.3 if len(segment) < 15 else -0.44
        if s == '?' and re.fullmatch(r'(?:right|okay|maybe|eh|you know|'
                                    r"don['’]t you think)", segment, re.I):
            return -2.5
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(text, token)
    return (doc, (text + token)[-800:]), value

"""Approximate a German-context activation, especially at word completions.

Recent words vote for German by their frequencies relative to eight other
European languages. German context gives a negative baseline, strengthened
by recognizable German words, prepositions, articles and ending-shaped pieces.
Capitalized pieces and vowel-free fragments weaken it. The first token
of a document has a separate positive German-spelling correction.
This captures a broad language signal, not individual subword quirks.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import numpy as np
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('de', 'en', 'nl', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'sv', 'pl')
PIECES = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+|[\W\d_]+')
PREPOSITIONS = set('''in im ins an am ans auf aus bei mit nach von vom vor
zu zum zur über unter um für durch gegen ohne seit zwischen hinter neben
wegen trotz gegenüber außer'''.split())
ARTICLES = set('der die das den dem des ein eine einen einem einer eines'.split())
ENDINGS = set('''en er es e em n s ung ungen lich liche lichen ig ige igen
isch ische ischen heit keit'''.split())

@lru_cache(60000)
def frequencies(word):
    return np.array([zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in LANGUAGES])

@lru_cache(100000)
def evidence(word):
    f = frequencies(word.lower())
    if len(word) < 2 or max(f) < 2.5:
        return np.zeros(len(LANGUAGES))
    return np.clip(f - max(f), -2, 0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        scores, word = np.zeros(len(LANGUAGES)), ''
    else:
        _, scores, word = carry
    new_word = not word or (bool(text) and not text[0].isalpha())
    for part in PIECES.findall(text):
        if part.isalpha():
            word += part
        else:
            if word:
                vote = evidence(word)
                if np.any(vote):
                    scores = .9 * scores + vote
                word = ''

    # Ambiguous or non-German evidence leaves the response near zero.
    current = scores + (evidence(word) if word else 0)
    probabilities = np.exp((current - max(current)) / 1.5)
    probabilities /= probabilities.sum()
    german = max(0., (probabilities[0] - .18) / .82)

    token = text.strip()
    lower = token.lower()
    letters = sum(c.isalpha() for c in token)
    capital = bool(token) and token[0].isupper()
    no_vowel = letters > 0 and not any(c.lower() in 'aeiouäöü' for c in token)
    whole = frequencies(word.lower()) if word else np.zeros(len(LANGUAGES))
    commonness = max(0., whole[0] - 2) / 5
    german_spelling = max(0., whole[0] - max(whole[1:]))

    value = german * (
        -.117 + .214 * capital + .103 * no_vowel
        -.166 * min(5, letters) / 5
        -.317 * commonness - .059 * german_spelling
        -.334 * (new_word and lower in PREPOSITIONS)
        -.177 * (new_word and lower in ARTICLES)
        -.166 * (lower in ENDINGS)
        -1.087 * (new_word and lower == 'in')
    )
    if first:
        f = frequencies(lower) if letters else np.zeros(len(LANGUAGES))
        value += .658 * max(0., f[0] - max(f[1:]))
    return (doc, scores, word), float(value)

"""German-text detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3011.

The component is near zero on most text but turns negative across German prose. Inside a
German sentence its activation is strongest on German function words (der, die, und,
von, mit, für, zu, auf, eine, ...) and weaker on other German words and endings; the same
word in English text ("in", "an", "so") gives about zero. So the size of the response
depends on how German the surrounding text is, not only on the current word.

The program keeps a running estimate of how German the current document is: an exponential
moving average (decay 0.95) over its tokens. A German function word or common German word
counts +1, a German ending (-ung, -lich, -en, -te, ...) +0.3, an umlaut or ß +0.5, an
English function word -0.3; ambiguous words (in, an, so, es, er) count 0 in the estimate.
The prediction is -1.0 times the estimate (only when it is positive), so it is 0 on English
and code and about -1 to -2 deep in German prose. Function words are scaled up by 1.5 and
punctuation down to 0.3. A new document resets the estimate.

Main idea in plain terms: "how German is this text so far", times "is this token a German
word that the model is reading as German".
"""

import re
import string

READS = ()

GERMAN_FUNCTION = set(
    "der die das und von mit zu zur zum für auf bei als eine einer einen einem eines dem den "
    "des ist sind wird werden wurde nicht auch nur nach über vor aus durch sie wir ich oder "
    "aber wenn dass sich ein noch wie hat haben sein seine ihre ihrem ihren bis um gegen ohne "
    "zwischen unter dann denn doch schon sehr man hier dieser diese dieses kann vom alle im".split()
)
GERMAN_CONTENT = set(
    "gibt geht gehen kommt kommen machen macht sagt sagte gab hatte jahr jahre jahren zeit "
    "mensch menschen mann frau kinder kind land stadt teil teile gut groß neue neuen neu alle "
    "allem allen vielen viele immer jetzt dort wieder mehr ganz selbst dabei bereits wer wo "
    "wann warum weil damit sowie etwa haus welt leben arbeit während seit heute müssen können "
    "wollen sollen jeder jede jedes andere anderen anderer also".split()
)
AMBIGUOUS = set("in an so es er".split())  # German or English
ENGLISH = set(
    "the and of to is that it for with on as are this be was by or not you he they we have has "
    "from which at there their these were been will would can about into more other when what "
    "them then than just also only very some such would could should been being where while each "
    "even because both here after before over under through during between without within".split()
)
GERMAN_ENDING = re.compile(r"(ung|lich|ungen|liche|igen|ige|chen|ten|en|nen|zen|enden|ende|te|isch|keit|heit|schaft)$")
GAIN = 1.0
DECAY = 0.95


def german_signal(word):
    """How German one token looks: +1 German word, +0.3 German ending, +0.5 umlaut or ß,
    -0.3 English word, 0 for ambiguous or other tokens."""
    if word in GERMAN_FUNCTION or word in GERMAN_CONTENT:
        return 1.0
    if word in AMBIGUOUS:
        return 0.0
    if len(word) >= 4 and GERMAN_ENDING.search(word):
        return 0.3
    if re.search("[äöüß]", word):
        return 0.5
    if word in ENGLISH:
        return -0.3
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    ema = 0.0 if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    ema = DECAY * ema + (1 - DECAY) * german_signal(word)
    scale = 0.3 if all(c in string.punctuation + " \n\t" for c in raw) else 1.0
    if word in GERMAN_FUNCTION:
        scale *= 1.5
    if word in AMBIGUOUS:
        scale *= 1.5
    return (doc, ema), -GAIN * max(ema, 0.0) * scale

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 3012.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
- Names of top-level system directories in absolute file paths, e.g. the "workspace" in
  "/workspace/project", "Users" in "/Users/name", "home", "local", "usr", "tmp", "opt".
  It is strongest right after a separate "/" token and weaker when the slash is glued to the
  name in one token ("/workspace").
- LaTeX line breaks (a double backslash "\\\\" in math) give a positive value.
- A double backslash inside an escaped code string (a backslash that is itself escaped, as
  in  print("\\\\n")  inside JSON or quoted code) gives a negative value.
- The "{\"" that opens a JSON object gives a small positive value.
Everything else is predicted as 0. This is a hand-written rule set; it captures only the
large, recognisable events and not the diffuse small activity elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

# activation when the directory name follows a separate "/" token
ROOT_DIRS = {"Users": 1.8, "local": 1.3, "home": 1.3, "workspace": 1.3, "opt": 1.2,
             "root": 1.1, "media": 1.0, "usr": 0.8, "share": 0.8, "tmp": 0.7, "etc": 0.6}
# the same names when the slash is glued to them in one token ("/workspace")
GLUED_SCALE = 0.5

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    ctx = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-40:-1])
    name = cur.lstrip("/")
    if name in ROOT_DIRS:
        if prev.endswith("/"):
            return None, ROOT_DIRS[name]
        if cur.startswith("/"):
            return None, GLUED_SCALE * ROOT_DIRS[name]
    if cur in ("\\\\", " \\\\") and ("\\n" in ctx or '\\"' in ctx):
        return None, -1.2
    if cur == " \\\\":
        return None, 1.8
    if cur == '{"':
        return None, 0.5
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3013: an "aim" detector.

It reads only the current token. It goes strongly negative on the English verb
"aim" in any capitalisation and its forms (aim, Aim, AIM, aims, aimed, aiming),
and weakly negative on the Cyrillic piece "им" when it sits inside a longer
word (вза|им|одействует). Every other token gives 0. The sizes are the average
activations measured on training text, so the program is a short lookup and
does not model the context that makes a given token stronger or weaker.
"""

READS = ()

# Average activation for each form of "aim", measured on training text.
AIM_FORMS = {"aim": -6.0, "aims": -4.6, "aimed": -4.0, "aiming": -5.7}

# Word-internal Cyrillic piece "им" (no leading space): weakly negative on average.
INNER_IM = -0.7


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in AIM_FORMS:
        value = AIM_FORMS[word]
    elif token == "им":
        value = INNER_IM
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3014 -- a "dl" / "ld" letter-pair detector inside split words.

What it does
    The component goes strongly negative on the letter pair L+D (spelled "ld", any case)
    when it sits inside a longer word that the tokenizer has split into pieces, e.g.
    "Mat|ild|is", "Hil|de|sheim", "Roths|child", "Gir|ald|us", "Mans|feld", "Chal|de|an",
    and on the boundary between two pieces, e.g. "Pagel|D", "Kill|d", "BAL|D".
    The size depends on the letter just before the L: after "a" it is strongest, after
    "i" or "e" moderate, after anything else (o, u, r, ...) weak. Whole common words
    ("should", "world", "build", "old") mostly stay near zero, and so do tokens that
    start with a space and are whole words.

How the program reads it
    It rebuilds the current word from the pieces seen so far in the document (letters
    since the last non-letter; a leading space starts a new word). If the word so far
    contains "ld" and the current piece is short (at most 4 letters), it predicts a
    negative value (-2.5 after a, -1.5 after i, -1.0 after e, -0.3 otherwise).

Why
    Activation is dominated by these rare large negative events; the rest is diffuse
    and not captured by a short program. Token identity alone reaches ~29% variance
    explained in cross-validation, and this rule reaches ~13% on training rows. A
    per-token lookup table would add some of the rest but has no concept behind it.
"""

READS = ()

# How negative the activation is, by the letter just before "l" in "...ld".
STRONG = {"a": 2.5, "i": 1.5, "e": 1.0}
WEAK = 0.3       # any other letter before "l" (o, u, r, start of word, ...)
MAX_PIECE = 4    # longer current pieces are usually whole words
SCALE = 1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word = "" if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry

    letters = piece.lstrip(" ")
    if not letters[:1].isalpha():
        return "", 0.0                       # punctuation, digits, newlines end a word
    # A piece with a leading space starts a new word; otherwise it continues the old one.
    word = letters if piece[:1] == " " else word + letters

    low = word.lower()
    at = low.find("ld")
    value = 0.0
    if at >= 0 and len(letters) <= MAX_PIECE:
        before = low[at - 1] if at > 0 else ""
        value = -SCALE * STRONG.get(before, WEAK)
    return word, float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 3015: a negative "n|it" / "nit" detector.

The component goes strongly negative when the letters n-i-t (and a few other
i-initial pieces) are spelled across a word-piece boundary, or as a whole
"nit"/"knit" piece. Everything else predicts 0.

  * "nit" or "knit" as a whole piece (S-nitrosylation, nitrobenzene, knit a
    scarf): strongly negative, about -6.
  * other pieces starting with "nit" or "knit" (nitrogen, nite, knitting):
    weakly negative, about -2.
  * a word-internal piece (no leading space, attached to the piece before it)
    that starts with "it" and follows a piece ending in "n", e.g. the "it" in
    "S-n|it|rosylation", "Magn|it|ogorsk", "chorioamnion|itis": about -3.
  * the same position with a piece starting "id", "is", "iz", "if", "ip",
    "ish", "ith", "ift", "ir", "iss", "il", "ix", "ih", "ij", "ig": about -1.
  * Cyrillic spellings of the same letters: after "н" (n), a piece "ит" (it)
    is about -1 and "из" (iz) about -3.

The "n" + "it" rule carries most of the score: it covers the large negative
outliers that dominate the component's variance.
"""

READS = ()

NIT_WHOLE = ("nit", "knit", "knits")
NIT_PREFIX = ("nit", "knit")
SECOND = ("id", "is", "iz", "if", "ip", "ish", "ith", "ift", "ir", "iss",
          "il", "ix", "ih", "ij", "ig")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    if word in NIT_WHOLE:
        return None, -6.0
    if word.startswith(NIT_PREFIX):
        return None, -2.0
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    attached = tok[:1].isalpha()
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if same_doc and attached and previous.endswith(("n", "н")):
        if word.startswith("it"):
            return None, -3.0
        if word[:2] in SECOND:
            return None, -1.0
        if word.startswith("ит"):
            return None, -1.0
        if word.startswith("из"):
            return None, -3.0
    return None, 0.0

"""A partial approximation of Chinese technical-vocabulary responses.

Apparatus, equipment and spending words receive positive scores; comparison,
sustainability and cooperation words receive negative scores. Physical-property
compounds are distinguished from abstract -ness. A few document-opening
conventions have separate scores, and most other tokens stay near zero.
Traditional characters are normalized; only the previous token is remembered.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from opencc import OpenCC

_converter = OpenCC('t2s')

def simplified(token):

# Endings for durability, corrosion resistance, heat/water resistance,
# elasticity, mobility, conductivity, modification and usability.

    '久', '腐蚀', '蚀', '热', '水', '磨', '弹', '韧', '粘',
    '黏', '动', '电', '燃', '改', '操作', '用',

    '#': -.899, '##': -.365, '#!/': -.54,

}

    elif word in {'配置', '装备'}:  # configuration and equipment
        value = .78
    elif word in {'费', '消费', '花费', '经费'}:  # fees and expenditure
        value = .77
    elif word == '性':  # concrete physical property versus abstract -ness
        value = .48 if physical else -.04
    elif word == '性能':  # performance, especially a physical compound
        value = 1.0 if physical else .48
    elif word == '好' and before in {'性能', '效果', '品质', '质量'}:

"""Arabic waw (و, "and" / "wa" / long "u") detector.

The component reads the Arabic letter waw inside the current token and sorts it by how
the waw is used. Standalone conjunctions و are strongly positive, as are waw-syllables
that end on a long vowel (وا, وي, وى); a waw that is followed by more letters
(وال, وان) is moderately positive, and a waw followed by a consonant (ور, ود, ول) is
almost silent. Tokens without a waw are predicted as 0.
"""
READS = ()

WAW = "و"
VOWEL_LETTERS = set("اىيی")  # alef, alef maksura, yeh, farsi yeh

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if WAW not in s:
        return carry, 0.0
    i = s.index(WAW)
    if s == WAW:
        return carry, 4.0            # standalone conjunction
    if i == len(s) - 1:
        return carry, 2.6            # waw ends the token, e.g. تو رو
    if s[i + 1] in VOWEL_LETTERS:
        if i + 2 == len(s):
            return carry, 4.8        # waw + long vowel ends the token, e.g. وا وي وى
        return carry, 1.8          # waw + vowel + more letters, e.g. وال وان
    return carry, 0.5               # waw before a consonant, e.g. ور ود ول

"""Indentation spaces that start a line of code (plus the first token of a document).

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3018 is sparse and weak: its activation is near zero
almost everywhere. Its clearest response is to a lone single-space token (" ") that comes
right after a line break, i.e. the indentation of a new line of code. The line break can be
a real newline, or an escaped one (a backslash followed by "n", as in code pasted inside a
JSON or JavaScript string); the escaped case is the stronger one.

Predictions:
- " " right after an escaped newline: 0.55
- " " right after a real newline:      0.21
- " " right after an opening quote:    0.25 (a space starting a string in code)
- first token of a document:           0.07 on average (the token's own value varies a lot)
  and a NUL character there: 2.7 (the rare extreme case)
- everything else:                     0

Only the last two characters of the text are carried from one position to the next.
"""

READS = ()

ESCAPED_LINE_START = 0.55  # " " after a backslash-n, in escaped code
LINE_START = 0.21  # " " after a real newline
QUOTE_SPACE = 0.25  # " " right after a " or ' mark
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.07  # first token of a document, on average
NUL_FIRST_TOKEN = 2.7  # a NUL character as the first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    before = "" if new_doc or carry is None else carry  # text of this document so far
    carry = (before + token)[-2:]
    if new_doc:
        return carry, (NUL_FIRST_TOKEN if token == "\x00" else FIRST_TOKEN)
    if token == " " and before.endswith("\\n"):
        return carry, ESCAPED_LINE_START
    if token == " " and before.endswith("\n"):
        return carry, LINE_START
    if token == " " and before.endswith(('"', "'")):
        return carry, QUOTE_SPACE
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3019 — a document-start component.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Almost all of the time it is quiet (activation near 0).
- On the first token of each document (the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first
  token of a row) it writes a token-dependent value, usually negative (about -0.2 on
  average). The value depends on the kind of token: capitalised words are the most
  negative, lowercase words and punctuation less so, digits and blank tokens near zero,
  and non-Latin-script words the most negative of all.
- The one large spike in the data: a "2" that immediately follows a "1" as the second
  token of a document fires at about +3.4.

Nothing here explains the component's small, diffuse, token-specific activity away from
document starts; that part is left at 0. Predicting it would need a per-token table.

The program keeps one number in its carry: the newest token's position within its own
document (0 for a document's first token), so it knows where each document starts.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation on a document's first token, by kind of token (from training rows).
START_VALUE = {
    "blank": -0.04,        # empty or whitespace-only token
    "digit": -0.07,        # 0-9 strings
    "upper": -0.29,        # starts with a capital letter, e.g. "The", "Car"
    "lower": -0.22,        # starts with a lowercase letter, e.g. "the", " and"
    "other_alpha": -0.36,  # non-ASCII letters (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, ...)
    "other": -0.15,        # punctuation, code symbols, special tokens
}

SPIKE = 3.4  # "1" then "2" as the first two tokens of a document


def kind(token):
    """The kind of a token, from its text alone."""
    text = token.strip()
    if not text:
        return "blank"
    if text.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if text[0].isalpha() and not text.isascii():
        return "other_alpha"
    if text[0].isupper():
        return "upper"
    if text[0].islower():
        return "lower"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token. `carry` is the position inside the current document
    of the previous token (None at a row's start)."""
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    new_document = t == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    position_in_document = 0 if new_document else carry + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if position_in_document == 0:
        value = START_VALUE[kind(token)]
    elif position_in_document == 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "1" and token == "2":
        value = SPIKE
    return position_in_document, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3021: a word-piece "-ness" detector.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
- Strongly NEGATIVE on a word piece spelled "ness" or "nes" that continues the word
  before it (no leading space): "even|ness", "wild|ness", "Wed|nes|days", "Hay|nes",
  "K|ness|et". Typical value about -2.5, sometimes -8 to -12. The same letters as a
  whole word with a leading space (" Nes", " Ness") are also negative, and so are the
  words " fitness" (about -4.5) and "NESS". Whole English words that merely end in
  "-ness" (" business", " thickness", " darkness") stay near zero.
- Mildly NEGATIVE on other "-ess" word pieces ("Bown|ess", "gumm|ess", "slown|ess").
- Mildly POSITIVE on short "n + vowel" word pieces such as "ni", "nil", "né", "nia",
  "nek", "eni". The clearest cases are Hungarian verb infinitives ending in -ni
  (tenni, foglalkoztatni) and Hungarian "né-" words (négy, német); " né" as a whole
  word is the strongest positive case.
- A small constant offset (+0.14) on the first token of each document, where the
  model has no context yet.
- Zero everywhere else, which is most tokens.

It reads only the newest token and the document labels, so it is causal by
construction. It is a token-level approximation: it captures the big events, not the
context-dependent size of each one.
"""

READS = ()

NESS_PIECES = {"ness", "nes"}  # the -ness spelling, as a piece or a whole token
ESS_PIECES = {"ess", "iss", "isse", "oss"}  # weaker "-ess" pieces
NI_PIECES = {"ni", "nil", "né", "nia", "nek", "nak", "eni", "nit"}  # n + vowel pieces
FITNESS_WORDS = {"fitness", "Fitness"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # First token of a document: no context, small positive offset.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.14

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    piece = word.lower()
    glued = not token[:1].isspace()  # a word piece that continues the word before it

    if glued and piece in NESS_PIECES:
        value = -2.5
    elif glued and piece in ESS_PIECES:
        value = -0.8
    elif glued and piece in NI_PIECES:
        value = 1.0
    elif word == "né":
        value = 3.0
    elif word in FITNESS_WORDS:
        value = -4.0
    elif piece in NESS_PIECES:
        value = -2.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Document-start detector for layer 1, MLP down-projection component 3023.

What it does: this component is silent almost everywhere. Its one large, regular
behaviour is at the first token of each document: the token that comes right after
a document break (an <|endoftext|> or a change of document id) and the first token of
each packed row. There the component is strongly negative, about -0.63 on average
(typically between -0.2 and -1.5). At that position the model has no earlier context
to look back on, so the value is set by which token it is; the program does not model
that per-token spread and predicts the average. Everywhere else it predicts 0.

Why: a document's first token starts a fresh attention window, so its activation
cannot depend on the text before it. Predicting the average at those positions
captures about 39% of the variance in the activation on training rows.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation over first-of-document tokens, measured on training rows.
DOC_START_VALUE = -0.63


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict this component's activation at the newest token.

    Returns carry unchanged (None): the rule needs only the last two document ids.
    """
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first_of_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return None, (DOC_START_VALUE if first_of_document else 0.0)

"""Short-term repetition: repeated words and identifiers give negative values.

Common words, grammar, code declarations and contractions count less.
Numbers and word continuations rely more on repeated two-token sequences
than on isolated pieces. Memory fades over a few dozen tokens and resets
at document boundaries. Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace;
capitalization and word starts additionally adjust single-letter weights.
This approximation does not reproduce rare large positive responses.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import get_frequency_dict

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('en', 'de', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'ru', 'ar', 'ko', 'zh', 'ja')
GRAMMAR = set(
    'the of and to is that or as be are was were been being am than but nor'.split()
)
DECLARATIONS = set(
    'import from def class public private protected static const function '
    'var let new using package namespace void include return extends'.split()
)
# Baseline and maximum repetition response, by recognizable text category.
RESPONSE = {
    'word': (0.014, 2.46),
    'number': (0.055, 1.53),
    'whitespace': (0.104, 0.16),
    'opening': (0.143, 0.96),
    'closing': (0.043, 0.04),
    'operator': (0.153, 0.55),
    'other': (0.007, 0.41),
}


def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + math.exp(-x))


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def properties(text):
    key = text.strip().casefold()
    weight = 1.0
    if any(c.isalpha() for c in key):
        word = key.strip('._-')
        frequency = max(
            max(0.0, 9 + math.log10(get_frequency_dict(lang).get(word, 1e-9)))
            for lang in LANGUAGES
        )
        # Very frequent words are mostly grammatical glue, not new content.
        weight = 0.035 + 0.965 * sigmoid(2.48 * (6.79 - frequency))
        if len(key) == 1 and key.isascii() and key.isalpha():
            letter = sigmoid(0.48 + 1.75 * text.strip().isupper()
                             - 1.50 * text.startswith(' '))
            weight = max(weight, letter)
        kind = 'word'
    elif key.isdigit():
        kind = 'number'
    elif not key:
        kind = 'whitespace'
    elif key in ('(', '[', '{', '<'):
        kind = 'opening'
    elif all(c in '.,;:!?)]}，。；：！？、' for c in key):
        kind = 'closing'
    elif key in ("'", '"', '`', '-', '+', '=', '*', '/', '|', '&', '^',
                 '~', '>', '\\'):
        kind = 'operator'
    else:
        kind = 'other'
    if key in GRAMMAR:
        weight *= 0.35
    if key in DECLARATIONS:
        weight *= 0.65
    if re.fullmatch(r"['’](s|t|re|ve|ll|d|m)", key):
        weight *= 0.17
    return key, kind, weight


def repetition(history, position, immediate_weight):
    strength = 0.0
    for earlier in history[-24:]:
        distance = position - earlier
        fade = (0.38 * math.exp(-distance / 12)
                + 0.09 * math.exp(-distance / 20)
                + 0.53 * math.exp(-distance / 32))
        strength += fade * (immediate_weight if distance < 4 else 1.0)
    return strength


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, {}, {}, '', '')
    _, mentions, phrases, previous_key, previous_text = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    key, kind, weight = properties(text)
    position = prefix.position
    history = mentions.setdefault(key, [])
    pair_history = phrases.setdefault((previous_key, key), [])
    short = 0.007 if kind == 'number' else 0.40
    strength = repetition(history, position, short)
    pair_strength = repetition(pair_history, position, short)
    blend = 0.0
    if text and previous_text:
        if text[0].isalpha() and previous_text[-1].isalpha():
            blend = 0.70
        elif text[0].isdigit() and previous_text[-1].isdigit():
            blend = 0.95
    strength = (1 - blend) * strength + blend * pair_strength
    baseline, peak = RESPONSE[kind]
    value = baseline - peak * weight * strength / (0.50 + strength)
    history.append(position)
    pair_history.append(position)
    return (doc, mentions, phrases, key, text), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3024: a "copied content word" detector.

The component goes negative when the current token repeats a content word that appeared a
short way back in the same document (about the last 50 tokens): repeated phrases,
test-runner output, code, lists and templates. Words are matched on their spelling, so
" serde" and "serde" count as the same word. It is about zero on first occurrences, on
punctuation and whitespace, and on common function words.

Strength depends on the kind of token: capitalised words and single letters (names and
variables) are strongest, ordinary words and digits are medium, and non-Latin script is
weaker. A repeat within the last 30 tokens counts fully; one 31 to 50 tokens back counts half.
"""

READS = ()

SCALE = 1.1
NEAR, FAR = 30, 50
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "a an the of to and or but is are was were be been being in on at by for with from "
    "as it its this that these those not no so if then than there here i you he she we "
    "they my your his her our their me him them us do does did can will would should "
    "could may might must have has had what which who when where how all any some each "
    "more most other into over under about up out just also only very one".split()
)


def _word(token_string):
    return token_string.strip()


def _strength(word):
    """How strongly a copy of this word drives the component; 0 for non-content tokens."""
    if not any(c.isalnum() for c in word) or word.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return 0.0
    if not word.isascii():
        return 0.65  # non-Latin script (CJK, Cyrillic, Greek, ...)
    if word.isdigit():
        return 0.75
    if len(word) == 1 or word[0].isupper():
        return 1.4  # single letters (variables) and capitalised names
    return 1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    words = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else []
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    words.append(word.lower())
    p = len(words) - 1
    value = 0.0
    # distance back to the most recent earlier occurrence of this word, within FAR
    for q in range(p - 1, max(-1, p - FAR - 1), -1):
        if words[q] == words[p]:
            if p - q >= 3:
                near = 1.0 if p - q <= NEAR else 0.5
                value = -SCALE * near * _strength(word)
            break
    return (doc, words), value

"""Explainer for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3026 (a rare, mostly-silent MLP output direction).

Almost everywhere this component is near zero (typical size 0.04). Its large values
come from two places:

1. The first token of a document (no earlier context in the document). There the
   value depends only on which token it is, and it is the same every time that token
   starts a document. The largest values are listed in DOCUMENT_START: strongly
   negative for "of", "and", "at", "Is", "Add", "Every", " total", " like", and
   strongly positive for " not", " it", and "//\\n". Other document-initial tokens get
   a small default of about -0.25. The list is a lookup of the 20 most influential
   document-initial tokens (ranked by value squared times frequency), not a general
   rule: surface properties such as case, script, digits, punctuation or length explain
   under 6% of the document-initial variance, so the rest of that variance needs the
   full per-token table.

2. A filler run of two middle dots "··" (token 60076), anywhere in a document: about
   -3.6, very consistent.

Everywhere else the program predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

FILLER = "··"  # two U+00B7 middle dots
FILLER_VALUE = -3.6

DOCUMENT_START = {
    " of": -5.4,
    "//\n": 10.3,
    " and": -2.5,
    " not": 5.2,
    "Is": -6.4,
    "Add": -6.9,
    " the": -0.9,
    " it": 3.1,
    " at": -3.1,
    "{\n": -6.9,
    "<|im_start|>": 0.5,
    "#ifndef": -4.6,
    "Every": -6.8,
    " total": -8.1,
    "和": -5.3,
    "Making": -3.7,
    "El": -4.2,
    "At": -4.2,
    " de": -2.8,
    " like": -4.8,
}
DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_START = -0.25


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_document = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    )
    if token == FILLER:
        return None, FILLER_VALUE
    if starts_document:
        return None, DOCUMENT_START.get(token, DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_START)
    return None, 0.0

"""A token-boundary detector for Indonesian words and affixes.

'Dengan' ('with') is strongly negative.  In Indonesian-looking text,
ber-/per- and consonant-bearing forms of meN-/peN- are mostly negative;
vowel-initial stems following men-/pen- are positive, especially when
the stem starts a new token.  Other words are mostly left at zero.
Repeated middle dots are a separate, positive formatting response.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Distinctive function words, plus nasal prefixes.  Avoid ambiguous cues
# such as 'dan' (also Dutch), 'para' (Spanish), and 'saat' (Turkish).
ID_CUES = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:yang|dengan|untuk|tidak|pada|adalah|dari|akan|'
    r'sebagai|oleh|dalam|karena|juga|menjadi|atau|saya|telah|'
    r'sudah|semua|lebih|tersebut|masih|harus|setelah|sebelum|'
    r'hingga|sehingga|tentang|kepada|bagi|terhadap|hanya|dapat|'
    r'banyak|melalui|namun|bahwa|mereka)\b|\b(?:meng|peng|meny|peny)\w{2}',
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WORD_END = re.compile(r'[a-zA-Z]+$')
NASAL_START = re.compile(r'(?:men|pen)([aeiou]).{0,2}$')

# Short token fragments starting Indonesian prefixed words.
PREFIXES = {
    'ber': -2.6, 'per': -3.1, 'mem': -2.8, 'meng': -2.0,
    'mer': -2.5, 'mel': -0.9, 'peng': -1.3, 'meny': 1.5,
    'peny': 3.0, 'dip': -2.4, 'dib': -2.1, 'pen': 1.3,
}
VOWEL_STEM = {'a': 4.8, 'e': 7.0, 'i': 3.2, 'o': 1.5, 'u': 7.0}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    recent = (tail + token)[-200:]
    match = WORD_END.search(tail)
    partial_word = match.group().lower() if match else ''
    at_word_start = not partial_word or token[:1].isspace()
    value = 0.0

    if word == 'dengan':
        value = -5.5
    elif partial_word == 'd' and word == 'engan':
        value = -6.5
    elif len(word) >= 2 and set(word) == {'·'}:
        value = 1.35
    elif ID_CUES.search(recent):
        if at_word_start and word in PREFIXES:
            value = PREFIXES[word]
        elif at_word_start and word in {'dari', 'demi'}:
            value = -0.8 if word == 'dari' else -4.0
        elif at_word_start and (nasal := NASAL_START.fullmatch(word)):
            value = 0.5 * VOWEL_STEM[nasal[1]]
        elif partial_word == 'mem' and word == 'per':
            value = -2.8
        elif not at_word_start and word[:1] in VOWEL_STEM:
            if partial_word in {'men', 'pen'}:
                value = VOWEL_STEM[word[0]] * min(1.0, 4.0 / len(word))
            elif partial_word == 'meny':
                value = 4.0 if word.startswith('e') else 0.8
    return (doc, recent), value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3027: an Indonesian verb-prefix detector.

What it does, in plain terms
- It is silent in nearly all text. It only speaks up inside Indonesian text, and there it
  responds to the start of Indonesian words built on verb prefixes and prepositions:
    * "dengan" (with) and "demi" (for the sake of): strongly negative (about -6 to -7);
    * "per", "mem", "ber", "meng", "dip", "dib", "dil", "peng", "mer" as the first piece of a
      word: moderately negative (about -1.5 to -3.5).
- Inside a word split after a bare men-/pen- prefix (e.g. "men" + "ur" + "ut" = menurut,
  "meny" + "eb" + "ut" = menyebut), the next piece is strongly positive (about +3 to +5).
- "Indonesian text" is judged per document: an Indonesian function word (yang, dan, untuk,
  tidak, ...) must have been seen at least three times so far, and outnumber English function
  words (the, and, of, ...) by two to one. Documents reset at each document boundary.

The rules are read off the component's activations on training text; they reproduce its
large, rare spikes and nothing of its small everyday noise.
"""

INDONESIAN_WORDS = frozenset(
    "yang dan ini itu untuk tidak akan dengan dalam adalah oleh juga bisa telah sudah "
    "kita saya mereka atau sebagai secara karena jika harus lebih bagi antara serta "
    "hingga tersebut bahwa kami anda setelah masih sangat orang dapat kemudian namun "
    "seperti menjadi hanya kalau maka tanpa semua".split()
)
ENGLISH_WORDS = frozenset(
    "the and of to is in that for with as on are by this be it was at from or an have "
    "not but which their they he she you we his her has had been were".split()
)
# Word-initial pieces in Indonesian text and their typical activation.
FIRST_PIECE = {
    " dengan": -6.0, " demi": -6.5, " per": -3.0, " Per": -3.0, " mem": -2.8,
    " ber": -2.6, " meng": -2.0, " dip": -2.2, " dib": -2.0, " dil": -1.4,
    " peng": -1.4, " mer": -3.5,
}
# Bare men-/pen- prefix pieces; the piece after one is a verb stem (positive).
PREFIX_PIECE = {" men": 4.0, " meny": 3.0, " pen": 3.0, " peny": 3.0}
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, 0)  # document id, Indonesian and English word counts so far
    _, n_id, n_en = carry
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if word.startswith(" "):
        plain = word.strip().lower()
        n_id += plain in INDONESIAN_WORDS
        n_en += plain in ENGLISH_WORDS
    carry = (doc, n_id, n_en)

    if word == " dengan":  # "dengan" is Indonesian (or Malay) whatever the surrounding text
        return carry, -6.0
    if not (n_id >= 3 and n_id > 2 * n_en):
        return carry, 0.0
    if word in FIRST_PIECE:
        return carry, FIRST_PIECE[word]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if before in PREFIX_PIECE and not word.startswith(" "):
        return carry, PREFIX_PIECE[before]
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3029 -- the "such a" / "such that" component.

What it does: it reads the word right after "such" and writes a strong signal that
separates the two readings of "such":

  "such a" / "such an" / "Such a"   ->  strongly positive (about +7)
  "such that"                       ->  strongly negative (about -5)

Weaker cousins of the same pattern: "way that" (about -2.6), "quite a/an" (about +1.8),
"so that" (about -0.6). Everywhere else it sits near zero. Its small, token-specific
wiggles (words starting with "ch" such as "chord" or "charity", a few other words) are
not modelled: they have mixed signs and no simple concept behind them.

Only the previous and current token are read, and a previous token from another
document does not count, as the model resets context at a document boundary.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = ""
    if len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()

    value = 0.0
    if prev == "such":
        if cur in ("a", "an"):
            value = 7.0
        elif cur == "that":
            value = -5.0
    elif prev == "way" and cur == "that":
        value = -2.6
    elif prev == "quite" and cur in ("a", "an"):
        value = 1.8
    elif prev == "so" and cur == "that":
        value = -0.6
    return carry, value

"""Adjective endings in -lar (-ular, -olar, -alar), e.g. "particular", "polar",
"solar", "angular", "circular", "stellar", "popular".

The component fires on the token that completes (or sits inside) a word ending
in the letters "lar". It is strongest on the Latin-style adjective endings
"-ular" / "-olar" / "-alar" and weaker on other "-lar" words, on words with
"lar" in the middle ("particularly", "larval"), and near zero everywhere else.

The program tracks the letters of the current word within its document (the
word resets at a document boundary or at any non-letter) and predicts a value
from the word's ending. It has no table of tokens: only the spelling of the
word so far.
"""

READS = ()


def _word_end(piece):
    """The letters at the end of a token piece (what a word-so-far ends with)."""
    j = len(piece)
    while j > 0 and piece[j - 1].isalpha():
        j -= 1
    return piece[j:], j == 0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ""
    tail, whole = _word_end(prefix.token_strings[-1].lower())
    # a token made only of letters extends the word; otherwise the word restarts
    word = word + tail if whole else tail
    if word.endswith(("ular", "olar", "alar")):
        value = 2.2
    elif word.endswith("ilar"):
        value = 0.5
    elif word.endswith("lar"):
        value = 1.5
    elif "lar" in word:
        value = 0.4
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, word), value

"""Adjective-stem ending detector (v2).

The component is negative on the piece that finishes an adjective whose stem
ends in an adjective-forming suffix: Greek -ικ- (Γενικ|ά, Φιλικ|ό), Russian
-ич-/-ск-/-ки-/-ик- (арктич|еской, ...), Latin/Romance -ic-/-ik- (economic|as,
Pontif|ical). It is near zero everywhere else, including on words that are
complete on their own. The strength depends on the stem: Greek -ικ- is
strongest, the others milder.

Only the word typed so far matters: the stem is the letters of the current
word before the newest token, within the same document.
"""

READS = ()

# stem ending -> predicted activation on the piece that completes the word
STEM_VALUES = {
    "ικ": -5.0,  # Greek -ικ-: adjective ending follows (Γενικ-ά)
    "ич": -0.9,  # Russian -ич-
    "ск": -0.9,  # Russian -ск-
    "ки": -0.9,  # Russian -ки-
    "ик": -0.5,  # Russian -ик-
    "ic": -0.5,  # Latin/Romance -ic-
    "ik": -0.5,  # Latin/Romance -ik-
}


def stem_so_far(prefix):
    """Letters of the word before the newest token, back to the word's start."""
    if not prefix.token_strings[-1][:1].isalpha():
        return ""
    stem = ""
    i = len(prefix) - 2
    while i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        piece = prefix.token_strings[i]
        if piece[:1] == " " or not piece.isalpha():
            break
        stem = piece + stem
        i -= 1
    return stem.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    stem = stem_so_far(prefix)
    value = 0.0
    for ending, activation in STEM_VALUES.items():
        if stem.endswith(ending):
            value = activation
            break
    return None, value

"""Christ and crystal spellings (positive), drill and grill spellings (negative).

Layer 1, one MLP hidden unit, written into the residual stream by down_proj. The
activation is read off the token that spells a word, so the program tracks the letters
of the word being spelled, which carry over from one token to the next.

- The name Christ, spelled Christ, Crist, Krist, fires strongly (+5). Chris and Kris
  fire less (+2.5). A short suffix that continues Christ, as in "Christi", also fires
  (+5). Christian, Christmas and Christopher do not.
- Crystal fragments (cryst..., ystal) and the bare pieces rist, rift, ift, ris, yst fire
  weakly (+2). Cyrillic Христ, Крист fire as Christ does.
- A word that ends in -ril or -rill (drill, grill, krill, nostril, Cyril) pushes strongly
  negative (-5), on the token that completes the spelling. April, brilliant, thrill and
  trillion do not. Only the completing token gets the value.
- Everything else is 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

CHRIST = re.compile(r"christ|crist|krist|kris|chris|^(христ|крист|рист)")
STRONG_CHRIST = re.compile(r"christ|crist|krist|^(христ|крист|рист)")
NOT_NAME = re.compile(r"christian|christmas|christopher")
CRYSTAL = re.compile(r"cryst|ystal")
PIECES = {"rist", "rift", "ift", "ris", "yst"}
RIL = re.compile(r"rill|ril$")
NOT_RIL = re.compile(r"brilliant|thrill|trillion|pril$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the letters of the word being spelled, up to the previous token
    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    base = word if tok[:1].isalpha() else ""
    spelled = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", base + tok).group(0).lower()
    low = tok.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    if CHRIST.search(low) and not NOT_NAME.search(low):
        value = 5.0 if STRONG_CHRIST.search(low) else 2.5
    elif CHRIST.search(base) and low in {"i", "ie", "o", "a"}:
        value = 5.0
    elif CRYSTAL.search(low) or low in PIECES:
        value = 2.0
    if RIL.search(spelled) and not NOT_RIL.search(spelled) and not (
        RIL.search(base) and not NOT_RIL.search(base)
    ):
        value = -5.0
    return spelled, value

"""Long-vowel "ee" detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3033.

What it does: the component fires on the letters of a word that spell the long-e
sound "ee" (see, tree, deep, Lee, Beef ...), and most strongly when the "ee" is split
across two tokens in an unfamiliar or short word, e.g. "Be" + "es" (Bees), "He" + "e",
"Ne" + "en", "Hame" + "ed" (Hameed), "Se" + "eb". The split case is where the big
activations are; "ee" inside one whole word (" see", " tree") is weak; words where
"ee" is an ordinary spelling (employees, freedom) do not fire.

How: rebuild the word the current token belongs to (its letters so far, from the
tokens before it in the same document), then score by where the "ee" sits.
"""

READS = ()


def _word_so_far(prefix):
    """Letters of the word ending at the current token, and the part before it."""
    pieces = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    cur = pieces[t].strip(" ").lower()
    before = ""
    # A token with no leading space that starts with a letter continues a word.
    if not pieces[t].startswith(" ") and pieces[t][:1].isalpha():
        parts = []
        j = t - 1
        while j >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[j] == prefix.document_ids[t]:
            s = pieces[j]
            if not s.strip(" ")[:1].isalpha():
                break
            parts.insert(0, s.strip(" ").lower())
            if s.startswith(" "):  # the first piece of the word
                break
            j -= 1
        before = "".join(parts)
    return cur, before


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur, before = _word_so_far(prefix)
    word = before + cur
    if "ee" not in word:
        return carry, 0.0
    if "ee" not in before and "ee" not in cur:
        # the "ee" straddles the token boundary: "Be" + "es"
        return carry, 3.3 if len(word) <= 5 else 1.0
    if "ee" in cur and "ee" not in before:
        # "ee" inside the current piece: a fragment ("Bee", "Lee") or a whole word (" see")
        whole = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position].startswith(" ")
        return carry, 0.2 if whole else 0.6
    return carry, 0.4

"""Copy-word detector (layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3035).

This component writes a strong *negative* signal on the token that spells the word
"copy": " copy", "Copy", "copies", "copied", "copier", the "cop" piece in "cop-ier" or
"Cop-ied", "photocopy", "zerocopy", "_copy", ".copy", and on the copy-stem in other
languages (Russian "коп" as in "копия", German "Kopie", Spanish/Italian "copia"; Chinese
"拷贝", Japanese "コピー"). It is strongest on "a copy" ("obtain a copy of the License"),
and on the "of" right after "copy" / "copies" / "copied" ("a copy of"). It is silent on
"copyright", "copper", "scope", and on almost everything else.

The program tracks the letters of the current word (letters since the last space or
punctuation), so a word split over several tokens is still recognised at the token that
completes it. Everything it predicts is negative or zero.
"""

READS = ()

# Predicted activation for a word whose letters so far are exactly this.
COPY_WORDS = {
    "copy": -6.0,
    "copies": -4.0,
    "copied": -4.0,
    "copying": -2.5,
    "copier": -8.0,
    "cop": -3.0,
    "kop": -4.0,
    "kopie": -6.0,
    "copia": -6.0,
    "коп": -10.0,
    "копия": -8.0,
    "копии": -9.0,
    "копию": -8.0,
    "копировать": -8.0,
    "拷贝": -8.0,
    "コピー": -8.0,
}
# Words that end in a copy-stem (photocopy, zerocopy, deepcopy, ...).
COPY_ENDINGS = ("copy", "copied", "copies", "copier", "copying")


def _letters(s):
    return "".join(c for c in s.lower() if c.isalpha())


def _value(word, prev_token, token):
    if word in COPY_WORDS:
        if word == "copy" and prev_token.strip() in ("a", "A"):
            return -8.0  # "a copy" is stronger than "copy" as a verb
        return COPY_WORDS[word]
    # "scopy" and "copyright" are not copy-words
    if word.endswith(COPY_ENDINGS) and not word.endswith(("scopy", "copyright")):
        return -5.0
    if word.endswith("коп"):
        return -8.0
    if word.endswith("cop"):
        return -3.0
    # the "of" in "a copy of", "copies of", "copied of"
    if prev_token.strip() in ("copy", "copies", "copied") and token.strip() == "of":
        return -6.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word, last = carry if carry is not None else ("", "")
    # a token with no leading space or punctuation continues the current word
    if token[:1].isalpha() and word:
        word = word + _letters(token)
    else:
        word = _letters(token)
    return (word, token), _value(word, last, token)

Track the alphabetic control word following a backslash, across token splits.
Font, layout, macro-definition and chemistry commands have negative responses;
common arithmetic commands are left near zero.  A command can leave a smaller
response on its following punctuation.  Also recognize the $latex convention,
mathematical arrows, diff hunk headers, and unfinished four-byte characters.
"""

import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Control words grouped by their purpose. Partial words occur when a command
# is split between tokens (new + command, math + bf, display + style, etc.).
CONTROL_WORDS = (
    (-12.0, 'newcommand renewcommand providecommand'),  # macro definitions
    (-3.3, 'new renew provide'),
    (-8.0, 'color textcolor colorbox'),
    (-5.6, 'boxed fbox'),
    (-4.6, 'large Large LARGE huge Huge'),
    (-4.5, 'rule pars'),  # drawing a rule / custom parentheses
    (-7.5, 'pu'),  # mhchem physical units
    (-4.0, 'ce'),  # mhchem chemical expressions
    (-5.3, 'map'),  # start of mapping-arrow commands
    (-2.3, 'mathrm mathsf mathtt mbox hbox'),
    (-1.7, 'mathbf mathit textbf texttt textit boldsymbol emph'),
    (-0.7, 'mathbb mathcal mathscr mathfrak cal frak Bbb rm bf bm'),
    (-1.3, 'text textup textnormal textrm textsf textsc mathop'),
    (-1.6, 'operatorname hspace vspace hfill vfill phantom phant'),
    (-0.9, 'display label eqref foot footnote'),
    (-0.5, 'displaystyle textstyle scriptstyle footnotes footnotesize'),
    (-0.5, 'quad qquad xspace'),
    (-1.5, 'overset underset nonumber limits cancel'),
    (-0.5, 'vec hat widehat tilde widetilde overline overrightarrow'),
    (-0.8, 'rf lfloor rfloor hline'),
    (-2.5, 'Longrightarrow'),
    (-3.0, 'PageIndex'),  # page-index annotations

             for word in words.split()}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3037: a backslash line-break detector.

What it does
- It fires on the doubled-backslash token (two backslash characters, `\\`), with or
  without a leading space (` \\`). These tokens are LaTeX line breaks in math, and
  escaped backslashes inside code strings.
- The sign follows the context. If the recent text of the same document looks like a
  quoted string or code (a double or single quote, print/echo/printf, fmt., assert,
  return, include, console), the value is negative (about -0.75). Otherwise, in
  LaTeX-like text, it is positive: about +1.2 after a space, +0.5 without one.
- Every other token is predicted as 0. Other backslash tokens (a single backslash,
  a backslash-n pair, a backslash-quote pair) are near 0 in the data and are not predicted.

How it reads context
- It keeps the last 200 characters of the current document, reset at each new
  document, and reads the newest token only.

Caveats
- Most of this component's variance is diffuse background (activations of about
  +/-0.04 spread over ordinary tokens, with no simple pattern), so this program
  explains only a small share of the variance. Its main effect is on the backslash
  line breaks, which account for nearly all of the component's effect on the model's
  next-token predictions.
"""

BREAK_SPACED = " \\\\"       # a space, then two backslash characters

CODE_MARKS = ('"', "'", "print", "echo", "console", "printf", "fmt.", "assert", "return",
              "include")

MEMORY = 200                 # characters of recent text kept for the context check
CODE_VALUE = -0.75           # backslash escape inside code text
LATEX_BARE = 0.5             # backslash line break in LaTeX-like text, no space before
LATEX_SPACED = 1.2           # backslash line break in LaTeX-like text, after a space


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    recent, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        recent = ""  # a new document: forget the old context
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

            value = LATEX_SPACED
        else:

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 3047 (down_proj): a comma detector for clause breaks in CJK text.

It fires on commas. The fullwidth comma "，" and the enumeration comma "、" give a large
positive activation, provided the clause they close is long enough: right after a sentence
break or a very short phrase (e.g. "目前，" or "三月，") it is near zero or negative, and
after a clause of about ten or more characters it is near its maximum. The ordinary ASCII
comma "," is weak, and stronger when the text around it is mostly Chinese or Japanese.
Every other token predicts 0.

Clause length is counted in characters back to the last sentence break (。！？ ; or a
newline) in the same document.

import re

SENTENCE_BREAKS = frozenset("。！？!?;；\n")
CJK = re.compile(r"[぀-ヿ㐀-鿿＀-￯]")


def clause_chars(prefix):
    """Characters since the last sentence break, within the same document."""
    tokens, docs = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids
    n, i = 0, len(tokens) - 2
    while i >= 0 and docs[i] == docs[-1]:
        if any(ch in SENTENCE_BREAKS for ch in tokens[i]):
            break
        n += len(tokens[i])
        i -= 1
    return n


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in FULLWIDTH_COMMAS:
        # Short leading phrases give ~0 or negative; clauses of 10+ characters give the peak.
        n = clause_chars(prefix)
        return None, min(1.7, max(0.0, (n - 3) * 0.25))
    if token == ",":
        # ASCII comma: weak, stronger when the recent text is mostly CJK.
        recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-40:])
        cjk_share = len(CJK.findall(recent)) / max(1, len(recent))
        return None, 0.7 if cjk_share > 0.2 else 0.1
    return None, 0.0

  * Positive on the quantity/degree word " more" or " much" when it sits in a

    "much of", "to more sophisticated": the word follows a preposition or "a".

    ("one or more", "so much", "is more"), where the component stays quiet.

    appears as a single token: ".-", ".—", ".--", ".–" as in run-in headings and
    figure captions ("Fig. 2.-A branch", "CONCLUSION.—The ...").

    极, 相当, более) and on runs of middle dots "····" (leader dots).

"""Estimate a local separator-continuation signal, not a syntactic parse.

A comma or coordinator gives a negative pulse when another comma occurred
only a few tokens earlier. The pulse fades with the gap. Changes of comma
style, fused punctuation, numeric items, and interruptions weaken it.
After an Oxford comma, the coordinator echoes the comma's predicted pulse.

The enumeration endings etc and 等 additionally get a small negative offset.
State is reset at every document boundary.
"""
import math

READS = ()
COMMAS = {',': 4.0, '，': 1.5, '、': 4.6}
CONJUNCTIONS = set(
    'and or & y et und и e ou oder o en или och dan og và 和 及 或'.split()
)

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 100, '', False, False, 0., '')

    age = min(age + 1, 100)
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip()
    comma = next((c for c in COMMAS if c in text), '')

    if (conjunction and not text[:1].isspace()
            and previous[-1:].isalpha() and word not in {'和', '及', '或'}):

    if comma or conjunction or word in ENDINGS:
        amplitude = (COMMAS.get(word, 1.5) if comma else
                     3.6 if word in ENDINGS else 3.5)

        if age == 1:
            evidence *= 0.57
        if fused:
            evidence *= 0.53
        if word in COMMAS and not fused and kind and word != kind:
            evidence *= 0.05
        if interrupted:
            evidence *= 0.3
        if previous.strip().isdigit():
            evidence *= 0.84

            value = 0.8 * last_pulse
        if word in ENDINGS:

The carry keeps recent bytes and the last token, resetting per document.

import unicodedata

        value = 3.0

        value = 2.6
    elif s == '何':  # surname He, also the question word 'what'
        value = 1.4

    elif low in ('без', 'бес', 'бесп'):

        slavic = any(c in SLAVIC_LETTERS for c in context)
        slavic = slavic or bool(SLAVIC_FUNCTION_WORDS.search(context))

Here ? is one letter or digit in a transliterated word. New a?a patterns
and their following fragment get negative responses, strongest in Greek.
Punctuation closing an a label is also negative, especially at line starts.
Small spelling/position offsets, middle-dot leaders, and the two literal
opening formats 'What is' and 'Title:' account for additional observed cases.
This is not a model of the component's remaining token-specific variation.
"""

import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii

@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def spelling(token):
    roman = anyascii(token).lower()
    letters = ''.join(c for c in roman if c.isalpha())
    greek = any('GREEK' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in token)
    return roman, letters, greek


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token, doc = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', (), 0, '', False)
    _, previous, word, history, position, line, old_pattern = carry
    roman, letters, greek = spelling(token)
    continuation = bool(token and previous and not token[0].isspace()
                        and previous[-1].isalnum())
    word = word + roman if continuation else roman
    tail = re.search(r'[a-z0-9]+$', word)
    word = tail.group() if tail else ''
    pattern = bool(re.search('a.a', word[-len(roman)-2:]))
    repeated = word.count('a') >= 2
    current_a = 'a' in letters

    value = -0.000590 - 0.032054 * (position == 0)
    if greek:
        value += 0.009882
        value -= 0.613821 * pattern
        value -= 0.576852 * (old_pattern and continuation)
    else:
        value -= 0.089527 * (pattern and continuation)
        value -= 0.048104 * (old_pattern and continuation)
        value -= 0.019821 * (repeated and not continuation)
        value -= 0.047061 * (repeated and letters.startswith('a'))
        value -= 0.358286 * (letters == 'a' and 'a' in history)
    value += 0.031147 * (continuation and current_a and not repeated)

    label = (token.strip() in {'.', ')', ').', ':'}
             and previous.strip() in {'a', '(a', '[a'})

        value -= 0.305006
        if re.fullmatch(r'\s*(?:\d+[.)]\s*)?\(?a', line):
            value -= 0.265832

    if len(leader) >= 2 and set(leader) == {'·'}:
        value += 0.552078
    if position == 1:
        if previous == 'What' and token == ' is':
            value -= 0.946927
        if previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
            value -= 2.856090

    history = (history + (letters,))[-4:] if len(letters) <= 1 else ()
    line = (line + token).rsplit('\n', 1)[-1][-80:]
    carry = (doc, token, word, history, position + 1, line, pattern)
